client_situation.text: The RFP is issued by Empire State Development (ESD), a New York State economic development corporation whose mission is to promote a growing state economy, encourage business investment and job creation, and support diverse local economies through loans, grants, tax credits, real estate development and marketing.

ESD's Office of Strategic Workforce Development (OSWD) was created under Governor Hochul's April 2022 $350 million workforce development investment and is charged with aligning workforce efforts to employer needs and creating economic opportunity for unemployed, underemployed and underrepresented workers.

ESD identifies Artificial Intelligence as one of the state's highest-growth sectors, citing Cornell Tech research, companies using AI for analytics, automation and decision-making, and the state-backed Empire AI initiative.

ESD's stated pain point is that rapid AI advancement risks widening economic inequality because many well-paying AI jobs require specialized education and technical training that lower-income New Yorkers cannot access.
ESD also points to tech recruiting practices that favor students at elite schools and those with personal connections to prominent technology companies as a barrier AI Prep is meant to level.

ESD currently has no AI Prep program in place: OSWD is launching AI Prep as a new applied training program and seeks to award contracts to up to two qualified program administrators to develop the curriculum and administer it.

The procurement is subject to a restricted period under the Procurement Lobbying Law running until contract approval, during which respondents may contact only the designated contacts Julia Borukhov and Jordan Kaplan at AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov.

goal.text: ESD wants up to two program administrators to design the curriculum for and deliver AI Prep across two tracks: Track A "AI Prep 4 Internships" for low-income matriculating undergraduates and Track B "AI Prep 4 Jobs" for low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment.
Track A requires a comprehensive AI technology training program for low-income college students that includes paid internship placements and builds a talent pipeline for AI employers.

Track B requires an industry-informed AI training program, delivered as an accelerated course or bootcamp as an alternative to traditional degree programs, that connects low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment to full-time AI jobs.

Deliverables common to both tracks include targeted outreach and recruitment, an application and assessment process, online AI courses built with industry and researcher input, participant stipends and wrap-around supports such as mentors or success coaches, and employer relationship building to generate placements.

The contract runs for an initial term of up to 18 months, with possible renewal or extension based on performance, need and availability of funds, and the anticipated contract start date is January 1, 2026.
ESD will invest up to $2M per track, up to $4M total, to train and provide stipends for participants.

Awarded administrators must track and report data including applicant, enrollment and completion counts with low-income percentages, paid internship and full-time placement rates, participating colleges and employer partners, with the exact list set during contract negotiation.

success_criteria.text: Proposals are scored out of a maximum of 100 points by an ESD selection committee, allocated as Firm Qualifications 15, Experience 25, Project Plan 30, Cost of Services 20 and Diversity Practices 10.
The program must serve a minimum of 250 participants, with priority for applicants proposing to serve more than 400, and over 50% of participants must be low-income.
The majority of program graduates must secure paid internships or full-time employment in artificial intelligence or a closely related field.

The Project Plan must estimate annual performance on three metrics — total participants served, percentage of low-income participants completing the curriculum, and paid internship or full-time job placement rate — justified by historical experience or partner commitments.

Questions must be submitted by email to AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov by August 29, 2025, with ESD responses due September 12, 2025, and proposals are due by 2:00 PM ET on October 1, 2025, with late proposals rejected.
Interviews, if necessary, are scheduled for the first week of November 2025 and the successful respondent is to be announced on November 14, 2025.

Applicants must have experience in at least three of four domains to qualify: academic services to college students, administering high-tech accelerated training programs, serving low-income populations, and working in the New York market.
Cost matching is not required but earns additional points in scoring, and the extent of any match must be shown in the budget template.

constraints.text: Budgets exceeding $2M for one track or $4M for both tracks over the total contract period will not be considered, and indirect costs are not an allowable expense.

The budget must be mapped to the program duration and cover Staff Salary and Benefits, Wraparound Supports and the proposed participant stipend level, and other costs such as curriculum development, marketing and events.

Proposals must be uploaded as a two-part submission (separate Administrative and Technical Proposal subfolders in a main folder named "company name – RFP title – date of Submission") to the Dropbox at https://www.dropbox.com/request/AIPrep; fax, hardcopy and email submissions are not accepted.

The Administrative Proposal must include, in order, the Non-Collusive Bidding Certification, Conflict of Interest Attestation, State Finance Law §§139-j/139-k forms, Vendor Responsibility Questionnaire, Iran Divestment Act Statement, EO-16 and EO-177 certifications, OCSD-1/OCSD-2/OCSD-4 diversity forms, the Encouraging Use of NYS Businesses form, ST-220-CA or affidavit, and a W-9, and missing any may cause rejection.

The contract carries a 30% MWBE participation goal and a 6% SDVOB participation goal, requiring an MWBE Utilization Plan and an SDVOB Utilization Plan (Form OCSD-4) with the proposal and quarterly and monthly compliance reporting thereafter.

The selected respondent must carry Commercial General Liability of $1M per occurrence and $2M aggregate, Commercial Auto of $1M if a vehicle is used, Sexual Abuse and Molestation insurance of $1M, and statutory Workers' Compensation, Employer's Liability and Disability coverage, naming ESD as additional insured with a waiver of subrogation.

Appendix A "ESD IT Security Standard Brief" and Appendix B "Diversity Practices Questionnaire" are referenced by the RFP but their contents are not included in the RFP text, so bidders must obtain them separately.

Contractor staff are subject to ESD approval, staff continuity is expected through project completion, and any subcontracting not identified in the proposal requires prior written approval of the State Project Manager.

The client is Empire State Development ("ESD" or the "Corporation"). ESD's mission is to promote a vigorous and growing state economy, encourage business investment and job creation, and support diverse, prosperous local economies across New York State. It does this through the efficient use of loans, grants, tax credits, real estate development, marketing, and other forms of assistance.

In April 2022, Governor Kathy Hochul announced a $350 million investment for workforce development, including creation of the Office of Strategic Workforce Development (OSWD) within ESD; OSWD is charged with aligning workforce development efforts with employers' needs and priorities and helping create economic opportunities for unemployed, underemployed, and underrepresented workers while meeting labor needs of the state's highest-growth sectors. One such sector is Artificial Intelligence (AI), which is advancing rapidly and revolutionizing industries such as healthcare, finance, transportation, and manufacturing. New York State is described as a key hub for AI development, with institutions like Cornell Tech leading research, companies leveraging AI for data analytics, automation, and decision-making, and state-backed initiatives like Empire AI supporting AI-driven advancements in medicine, infrastructure, and cybersecurity. The document states that rapid AI advancement raises concerns about widening economic inequality, particularly for low-income individuals who may lack the skills or access needed to benefit from the AI-driven economy, since many well-paying AI-related jobs require specialized education and technical training often out of reach for lower-income individuals. By implementing AI Prep, New York intends to create opportunities in this sector while reinforcing its position as a hub for innovation and economic opportunity.

Under Governor Hochul's direction, OSWD is launching AI Prep, an applied training program aimed at expanding access to the specialized skills and opportunities needed for AI jobs. The program responds to tech recruiting practices that favor students at elite schools and those with personal connections to prominent technology companies; AI Prep aims to level the playing field by training low-income New Yorkers in cutting edge AI skills with the goal of connecting them with AI internships or jobs at leading New York tech companies. AI Prep has two dedicated tracks for New Yorkers currently underrepresented in the tech industry who cannot reasonably access training on their own: Track A, "AI Prep 4 Internships," provides low-income matriculating undergraduate students with AI training with the goal of securing paid internship opportunities at leading tech companies; Track B, "AI Prep 4 Jobs," connects low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment with AI jobs through an accelerated training or bootcamp that serves as an alternative to traditional degree programs. OSWD seeks to award contracts to up to two (2) qualified program administrators to develop the curriculum for and administer AI Prep for Track A and/or Track B.

Track A: AI Prep 4 Internships — the administrator must develop and deliver a comprehensive AI technology training program for low-income college students that includes paid internship placements, creating direct pathways from education to the AI industry and building a talent pipeline for AI employers. Administrator responsibilities include: targeted outreach and recruitment strategy for low-income students; a program application and evaluation process; needs assessments to identify and address student barriers; industry-informed AI curriculum design; delivery and management of the AI training program; participant stipends and wrap-around supports including mentorships and career coaches with industry expertise; and helping students secure paid internships. The administrator must also cultivate and maintain relationships with leading industry employers to inform training content and generate paid internship opportunities. The curriculum should consist of online AI courses developed with input from leading researchers and industry experts, with mentorship and real-world machine learning projects; the administrator should propose whether training is offered during the academic year or through summer courses, demonstrating alignment with employer internship hiring cycles/needs. Training should be tailored to help students secure paid internship placements with leading New York State technology companies, leading ultimately to full-time jobs.

The administrator must deliver an industry-informed, comprehensive AI technology training program that equips low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment with in-demand technical and professional skills and connects them to AI jobs. Required program elements: tailored outreach and recruitment strategy for unemployed, underemployed, and underrepresented New Yorkers; online AI courses with curriculum incorporating industry input on technical skills and learning milestones; a program application and assessment process; an immersive training schedule deliverable part-time or full-time; participant stipends and wrap-around supports including success coach staff; evaluation metrics to measure participant skill attainment during training; professional development support for trainees throughout training; credentials expected as a result of training completion (if applicable); and full-time job connection support in an AI-related field. The administrator is expected to cultivate and maintain relationships with leading industry employers to inform training content and generate full-time employment opportunities. ESD will invest up to $2M for each track (up to $4M total) to train and provide stipends for participating individuals, for an initial term of up to 18 months, with possible renewal or extension based on performance, need, and availability of funds.

New York State certified Minority- and Women-Owned Businesses ("MWBEs") and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Businesses ("SDVOBs") may request that their firm's contact information be included on a list of MWBE and SDVOB firms interested in serving as a subcontractor for this procurement. The listing will be publicly posted on the Contract Reporter and ESD's website for reference by potential Respondents. A firm requesting inclusion should send contact information and a copy of its NYS MWBE or SDVOB certification to AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov. Nothing prohibits an MWBE or SDVOB vendor from proposing as a prime contractor.

ESD anticipates selecting up to two program administrators to design and deliver the AI Prep program. Program objectives: serve a minimum of 250 participants, with priority for applicants serving more than 400 participants; over 50% of participants should be low-income; the majority of graduates should secure paid internships or full-time employment in artificial intelligence or a closely related field. Applicants must be organizations with a strong track record for workforce development in AI or similar fields. Applicants may form teams to increase competitiveness, but one organization must be the lead for the proposed programming.

Applicants to administer the program may be either non-profit or for-profit entities. Applicants must have experience in at least three of four domains to qualify: providing academic services to college students; administering high-tech accelerated training programs; serving low-income populations; working in the New York market.

ESD will fund up to an 18-month period for the selected administrator(s) to operate the AI Prep program. Applicants must detail their own budget and associated justification. Budgets exceeding $2M for one track or $4M for both tracks for the total contract period will not be considered. ESD has the right to review all expenses and deny reimbursement of any expenses deemed ineligible.

Applicants must submit a proposed budget mapped to the program duration, comprising: Staff Salary and Benefits; Wraparound Supports and Proposed Participant Stipend Level; and other costs deemed necessary for program success, including but not limited to curriculum development and implementation, marketing, and events. Indirect costs are not an allowable cost under this grant.

There is no cost-match requirement associated with this grant. Applicants will receive additional points associated with cost-matching during the scoring process. The extent of cost matching should be indicated in the budget template. A footnote states the proposed definition is eligible for, or in receipt of, Pell Grants, but applicants may propose and offer justification for an alternative definition.

Applicants awarded funding must track and record information relevant to the success of this grant, and data will be made available to ESD as requested. Data points to be captured and tracked are at the discretion of ESD, with the exact list determined during contract negotiation. Expected data points include: number of applicants and percentage that are low-income; number of participants who enroll and percentage low-income; number of participants who complete the program and percentage low-income; paid internship placement rate and percentage of placements for low-income students; full time job placement rate and percentage of placements for low-income individuals; participating colleges and universities; and participating employer partners.

The chunk lists the anticipated schedule of dates for this RFP: release of RFP on August 8, 2025; deadline for submission of questions on August 29, 2025; deadline for ESD to respond to questions on September 12, 2025; submission of proposals on October 1, 2025 by 2:00 PM ET; interviews (if necessary) in the first week of November 2025; announcement of successful respondent on November 14, 2025; anticipated contract start date of January 1, 2026; anticipated debriefing timeframe TBD. The Corporation reserves the right to change any of the dates stated in this RFP.

ESD shall establish a selection committee to evaluate Proposals. The selection committee will consider stated criteria and assign point values to each Proposal based on their evaluation. The maximum number of points any Proposal may receive is 100.

Section VI.A "Firm Qualifications" is worth 15 points in the Technical Proposal. Respondents must include a cover letter describing the organization's mission and history, annual budget, annual number of participants served, partnerships with employers, and motivations for applying to run AI Prep. Respondents must also describe how their organization delivers substantive, skill-based, college-level or accelerated immersive training in AI, which industry experts they partner with, and how they ensure the curriculum remains current and aligns with employer demand.

Section VI.B "Experience" is worth 25 points of the selection criteria; Respondents must demonstrate knowledge and ability to perform the services described in the RFP. Required experience descriptions: work with college students (if applicable), detailing length of training, number of students served, number of cohorts, cost per student, and internship and/or job placement rates of recent program graduates. Other participants: work training a high-tech workforce in AI and related fields (excluding college students), describing length of training, number of participants served, number of cohorts, cost per participant, and job placement rate of recent program graduates. Low-income individuals: work with low-income students or individuals, including number served and any additional supports provided. Employers: how the organization coordinates with individual employers to place participants in AI-related internships or jobs. New York: any work the organization does in the New York market.

Section VI.C "Project Plan" is worth 30 points of the Technical Proposal. Respondents must describe how their organization would administer the AI Prep program, including a monthly timeline from planning through completion of internships or full-time jobs by the first cohort, covering: curriculum development (or specify if already completed); recruiting participants for Track A or Track B; proposed training duration; proposed cohort size; proposed stipend level and/or other supports offered; and internship or full-time job placement. Respondents must also describe how AI Prep funding would expand similar existing programming, how many additional participants could be served, and how quality of current programming would be maintained or enhanced. Applicants for both Tracks must detail organizational capacity and strategy to manage two programs simultaneously per the RFP's expectations. Required attachments: 1-page resumes of key personnel involved in administering the program, and letters from partner employers demonstrating commitment to providing paid internships or full-time employment to graduates. Recruitment section must define low-income for the program's purposes, describe targeting for the applicable Track(s), and detail partnerships with nonprofits and any New York colleges or universities.

This chunk is part of the "C. Project Plan (30 Points)" selection criterion. It asks proposers to include details on any relevant partnerships their organization has with nonprofits and any New York colleges or universities. It asks proposers to describe how they currently measure and report program success and to estimate annual performance against three metrics: total number of participants served annually; percentage of low-income participants that complete the curriculum; and paid internship or full-time job placement rate of program graduates. Estimates must be justified based on historical experience and/or commitments from proposed program partners.

Cost of Services is worth 20 Points in the Selection Criteria (Section VI.D). Respondents must submit a line-by-line price proposal of proposed fees to accomplish the scope of work in this section of the Technical Proposal. Personnel Services (PS) costs must include job title, name of employee (if known), hourly rate or annual compensation rate, fringe rate, percentage of time dedicated to project, and cost to contract. Other Than Personnel Services (OTPS) costs must be listed each on a separate line with cost to contract and number of each item; examples given are hardware/equipment, software, training materials, insurance, participant stipends, and wrap-around services such as transportation assistance. A bracketed note states that in case of complex cost structure, the originator should establish a uniform schedule inclusive of all fee components.

ESD's Office of Contractor and Supplier Diversity will score each application for Diversity Practices. Up to 10 points will be awarded based on the contents of the Diversity Practices Questionnaire, Appendix B, submitted by each Respondent to the RFP.

ESD (referred to as "the Corporation") reserves the right to determine, in its sole discretion, whether reference checks for one or more Respondents will be necessary. Information provided by references may be used by the Corporation for proposal evaluation purposes. The Corporation may seek additional information from references on subjects including the quality of services provided, anticipated ability to perform the services required in this RFP, and the responsiveness of the Respondent to the client during the engagement. The Corporation reserves the right to deploy a variety of methods and communication approaches to contact references, at its sole discretion.

Section VII (Submission of Proposals) instructs Respondents to submit a proposal that clearly and concisely provides all requested information. Emphasis should be on conformance to the RFP instructions and requirements and on completeness and clarity of the proposal response. Respondents are advised to thoroughly read and follow all instructions in the RFP. Proposals that do not comply with these instructions or do not meet the full intent of all RFP requirements may be subject to scoring reductions during the evaluation process or may be deemed nonresponsive.

The Technical Proposal must be organized with bookmarks matching a specified listing: A. Cover page (including Respondent's contact information); B. Table of Contents; C. Firm Experience and Qualifications; D. Staff Experience and Qualifications; E. Project Plan and Approach; F. Cost of Services; G. Diversity Practices Questionnaire. Respondents are to provide no information beyond what is specifically requested. The purpose of the Technical Proposal is to let Respondents demonstrate their qualifications, competence, and capacity to undertake the engagement described in the RFP, in a manner complying with applicable laws and regulations and the requirements of the RFP.

The chunk lists the Administrative Proposal items Respondents must complete and submit, in the order listed, for the Corporation (ESD); failure to submit any may result in rejection of the proposal. Schedule A of the RFP states standard requirements that must be included in every contract with the Corporation, and the successful Respondent must agree to abide by them and provide any information requested. Required items: i. Non-Collusive Bidding Certification; ii. Conflict of Interest Attestation; iii. State Finance Law §§139-j and 139-k forms; iv. Vendor Responsibility Questionnaire (osc.ny.gov); v. Iran Divestment Act Statement; vi. Executive Order 16 Certification; vii. Executive Order 177 Certification; viii. Non-Discrimination and Contractor & Supplier Diversity Requirements (OCSD-1 MWBE and SDVOB Participation / EEO Policy Statement, OCSD-2 Staffing Plan, OCSD-4 MWBE and SDVOB Utilization Plan); ix. Encouraging the Use of NYS Businesses in Contract Performance Form; x. Certification under State Tax Law Section 5-a, Form ST-220-CA or Affidavit; xi. W-9 Form. Additional information about these items and ESD's procurement requirements is in Section X of the RFP ("Contractual Requirements").

Proposals must be submitted only as described in the RFP instructions; submissions by facsimile, hardcopy or email will not be accepted. Respondents must create a main folder named "company name – RFP title – date of Submission" (example: "ABDX, Inc. – AIPrepRFP – 08.08.2025") containing two subfolders, one for the Administrative Proposal and one for the Technical Proposal, with all documents clearly labeled. The main folder must be uploaded to Dropbox via the link https://www.dropbox.com/request/AIPrep using the option Add Files > Folders from computer. Proposals deemed to arrive late will not be considered for award.

Questions or requests for clarification must be submitted by email to AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov, citing the RFP page and section, in accordance with the schedule in Section V (Schedule of Dates). Questions are not accepted orally, and questions received after the deadline may not be answered. The comprehensive list of questions/requests for clarification and the official responses will be posted as an Addendum to this RFP. Respondents are strongly encouraged to review all posted questions and answers, through which ESD may offer clarifications or advise of material changes to the RFP.

ESD reserves rights including amending, modifying or withdrawing the RFP; revising requirements; requiring supplemental statements or information; accepting or rejecting any or all responses; extending the submission deadline; negotiating contract terms with any Respondent; clarifying non-conforming responses; cancelling or reissuing the RFP in whole or in part; and extending the term of any agreement on terms consistent with this RFP. ESD may exercise these rights at any time without notice and without liability for respondents' proposal preparation expenses; all costs of responding are borne solely by the Respondent. All information submitted in response is subject to the Freedom of Information Law ("FOIL"), and Proposals may be discussed at meetings of the ESD Directors, which are subject to the Open Meetings Law.

Contractor staff assigned to the project are subject to approval by the Corporation, and continuity of assigned staff until project completion is highly desirable. The Contractor must notify the Corporation immediately of any proposed staff changes; the Corporation has absolute right and discretion to approve or disapprove changes, and will be given a summary of the proposed substitute's experience and an opportunity to interview that person before deciding, with approval not to be unreasonably withheld. The Contractor represents that its members, officers, employees, agents, servants, consultants, shareholders and subcontractors possess the experience, knowledge and character necessary for their duties. The Agreement is intended to secure the Contractor's professional services because of its ability and shall not be assigned, conveyed, transferred or disposed of by the Contractor.

The Agreement resulting from this RFP is intended to secure the professional services of the Contractor because of its ability and shall not be assigned, conveyed, transferred, or disposed of by the Contractor. The Contractor agrees not to subcontract any of its services, unless as indicated in its proposal, without the prior written approval of the State Project Manager; approval shall not be unreasonably withheld upon receipt of a written request to subcontract. All employees of the Contractor or its Subcontractors performing Services must possess the necessary qualifications, training, licenses, and permits required in the jurisdiction where the Services are provided and be legally entitled to work in that jurisdiction. All persons, corporations, or other legal entities performing Services on behalf of the Contractor must comply with all applicable Federal and State laws concerning employment in the United States.

Section X ("CONTRACTUAL REQUIREMENTS") of the RFP provides additional information about the forms required in each Respondent's submission pursuant to Section VII of the RFP, and about ESD's procurement requirements. For this section, "bid" means any submission in response to this RFP, and "bidder" means any individual or entity that submits a "bid". The issuing body is referred to as ESD. The chunk references Section VII of the RFP as the source of the submission form requirements.

All bidders must certify, in accordance with Section 2878 of the New York State Public Authorities Law, that they have not colluded with any other Respondents in their proposal. The required Non-Collusive Bidding Certification form is available at https://esd.ny.gov/sites/default/files/media/document/NonCollusiveBiddingCertification6-1325.pdf. The certification must be completed and included in all proposals.

Respondents must attest they have read, understood and will comply with ESD's Conflict of Interest Attestation (https://esd.ny.gov/sites/default/files/Conflict-of-Interest-Attestation-June-2019.pdf); ESD may disqualify a Respondent or terminate any resulting contract if it determines the Respondent violated these requirements. Under "Gifts and Offers of Employment," Respondents have not and shall not offer any gift (money, services, loan, travel, entertainment, hospitality, thing or promise, or any other form) to any ESD employee, member or director during the procurement and contract negotiation where it could reasonably be inferred the offer was intended to influence or reward official action. Respondents may not make offers of employment or discuss such offers with any ESD employee, member or director involved in this procurement or resulting contract negotiation within at least 30 days from the time that employee's involvement closed. Under "Disclosure of Potential Conflicts," Respondents must disclose any existing or contemplated relationship with any other person or entity, including relationships with any member, shareholders of 5% or more, parent, subsidiary, or affiliated firm, that would constitute an actual or potential conflict of interest or appearance of impropriety relating to other clients/customers/employers of the Respondent or former ESD officers and employees, in connection with the services rendered.

Respondents must describe how they would eliminate or prevent any conflict of interest enumerated in the RFP. Respondents must disclose whether they, or any of their members, shareholders of 5% or more, parents, affiliates, or subsidiaries, have been the subject of any ongoing investigation or disciplinary action by the New York State Commission on Ethics and Lobbying in Government or its predecessor State entities ("Commission"). If so, a description must be included indicating how any matter before the Commission was resolved or whether it remains unresolved.

State Finance Law Sections 139-j and 139-k ("Procurement Requirements") apply to this RFP, governing permissible communications between potential Respondents and ESD or other involved governmental entities, requiring disclosure of persons or organizations whose function is to influence procurement contracts, public works agreements and real property transactions, and establishing sanctions including disqualification from award for knowing and willful violations. All communications regarding this RFP must be conducted only with the designated contact persons listed above, from issuance through final award and execution of any resulting contract (the "Restricted Period"). Respondents must submit as part of their submittal the Offeror Disclosure of Prior Non-Responsibility Determinations and the Offeror's Affirmation of Understanding and Agreement pursuant to State Finance Law, and must periodically update such forms during the term of any resulting contract. Copies of these forms are available at https://esd.ny.gov/sites/default/files/media/document/SF-Law139-JK-2025.pdf.

The chunk references State Finance Law Sections 139-j and 139-k forms, available at https://esd.ny.gov/sites/default/files/media/document/SF-Law139-JK-2025.pdf. ESD staff must obtain and report information when contacted by Respondents during the Restricted Period, make a determination of responsibility of Respondents, and make such information publicly available per applicable law. A Respondent found to have knowingly and willfully violated the State Finance Law provisions, along with its subsidiaries, related or successor entities, will be determined a non-responsible Respondent and will not be awarded any contract issued pursuant to this solicitation; two such findings of non-responsibility within a four-year period can result in debarment from obtaining any New York State governmental procurement contract. The designated contact account for this solicitation is referenced on the cover of this RFP. Both the prime consultant and any sub-consultants must complete the required forms.

All Respondents to this RFP must be "responsible," meaning they have the requisite financial ability, organizational capacity and legal authority to carry out obligations under the RFP, and must demonstrate that the Respondent and its principals have and will maintain the level of integrity needed to contract with New York State entities such as ESD; the Respondent must also show satisfactory performance of all prior government contracts. The contract between ESD and the Respondent, if any, shall include clauses that the Respondent remain "responsible" throughout the contract term, that ESD may suspend the contract if information calls into question the contracting party's responsibility, and that ESD may terminate the contract if the party is determined non-responsible; model language will be provided on request. ESD requires all Respondents to register in the State's Vendor Responsibility System ("Vend-Rep System"), a secure centralized database for Vendor Responsibility Questionnaire information; New York State Procurement Law requires state agencies to award contracts only to responsible vendors. Respondents must file the Vendor Responsibility Questionnaire online via the Vend-Rep System or submit a paper questionnaire, and must include a copy of the Vend-Rep submission receipt or paper questionnaire with the proposal; the Vendor Responsibility Questionnaire must have been completed within one year of proposal submission.

The Vendor Responsibility Questionnaire must have been completed within one year of proposal submission. Respondents must enroll in and use the Vend-Rep System at www.osc.state.ny.us/vendrep; the Office of the State Comptroller's Help Desk is reachable at 866-370-4672 or 518-408-4672 or itservicedesk@osc.state.ny.us. Respondents opting to file a paper questionnaire can obtain it from the Vend-Rep website (http://www.osc.state.ny.us/vendrep/forms_vendor.htm) and must complete the questionnaire matching their business activity ("Construction" or "Non-Construction") and business type ("For-Profit" or "Not-for-Profit") from four (4) available options. The chunk also links to EO-192: https://ogs.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2021/09/eo192-vendor-integrity_0.pdf.

Chunk covers New York State Executive Order 16 ("EO-16"), which prohibits State Agencies and Authorities from contracting with businesses in Russia; EO-16 remains in effect while federal government sanctions are in effect. All bidders must certify compliance with EO-16, including each party to a joint bid certifying as to its own organization, under penalty of perjury. The required certification is at https://esd.ny.gov/sites/default/files/EO16-certification.pdf and must be signed and included in all Proposals.

All bidders must certify compliance with New York State Executive Order 177 and the New York State Human Rights Law, which prohibits discrimination and harassment based on a protected class and requires reasonable accommodation for persons with disability or pregnancy related conditions. The required certification is at https://esd.ny.gov/sites/default/files/EO-177-Certification.pdf. The certification must be signed and included in all Proposals.

The chunk states that ESD (Empire State Development) is required, pursuant to New York State Executive Law Article 15-A and Parts 140-145 of Title 5 of the New York Codes, Rules and Regulations, to promote opportunities for maximum feasible participation of New York State-certified Minority and Women-owned Business Enterprises ("MWBEs") and the employment of minority group members and women in the performance of ESD contracts. It is a contractual requirement under the section "Non-Discrimination and Contractor & Supplier Diversity Requirements."

ESD establishes an overall goal of 30 percent for MWBE participation in this solicitation, based on current availability of MBEs and WBEs. A Contractor on any resulting Contract must document good faith efforts to provide meaningful participation by MWBEs as subcontractors and suppliers; by submitting a response, the Respondent agrees ESD may withhold payment pending receipt of required MWBE documentation. The MWBE directory is at https://ny.newnycontracts.com, and guidance on evaluating "good faith efforts" is in 5 NYCRR § 142.8. Only sums paid to MWBEs for a commercially useful function (as defined in 5 NYCRR § 140.1) count toward the goal; for construction contracts an MWBE supplier counts as 60 percent of total contract value and a broker as the fees or markup charged, while for all other contracts an MWBE broker counts as 25 percent of total contract value.

Chunk sets MWBE participation compliance rules for contracts resulting from this RFP. For all other contracts, the portion of a contract with an MWBE serving as a broker deemed to represent the commercially useful function performed by the MWBE is 25 percent of the total value of the contract. Per 5 NYCRR § 142.13, a finding that the Respondent willfully and intentionally failed to comply with MWBE participation goals constitutes a breach of contract and ESD may withhold payment as liquidated damages, calculated as the difference between (1) all sums identified for payment to MWBEs had the Contractor achieved the contractual MWBE goals and (2) all sums actually paid to MWBEs for work performed or materials supplied under the Contract. By submitting a proposal, a Respondent agrees to demonstrate good faith efforts to achieve applicable MWBE participation goals by submitting evidence through the New York State Contract System ("NYSCS") at https://ny.newnycontracts.com, or via a non-electronic method by contacting the Office of Contractor and Supplier Diversity ("OCSD") at OCSD@esd.ny.gov. Respondents must submit an MWBE Utilization Plan with their proposal; modifications or changes to an accepted MWBE Utilization Plan after Contract award and during the Contract term must be reported on a revised MWBE Utilization Plan and submitted to ESD for review and approval, and ESD will advise of acceptance or issue a notice of deficiency within 30 days of receipt.

ESD reviews the submitted MWBE Utilization Plan and advises the Respondent of acceptance or issues a notice of deficiency within 30 days of receipt. If a notice of deficiency is issued, the Respondent must respond within seven (7) business days by submitting a written remedy to OCSD at OCSD@esd.ny.gov; if the remedy is untimely or inadequate, ESD directs the Respondent to submit a request for partial or total waiver of MWBE participation goals within five (5) business days, and failure to file the waiver form timely may be grounds for disqualification. ESD may disqualify a Respondent as non-responsive if it fails to submit an MWBE Utilization Plan, fails to submit a written remedy to a notice of deficiency, fails to submit a request for waiver, or if ESD determines the Respondent failed to document good faith efforts. The successful Respondent must attempt in good faith to utilize any MBE or WBE identified in its MWBE Utilization Plan during Contract performance; waiver requests after Contract Award may be made at any time during the Contract term but no later than prior to submission of a request for final payment. The successful Respondent must submit a quarterly MWBE Contractor Compliance & Payment Report to ESD by the 10th day following each end of quarter over the Contract term documenting progress toward the MWBE goals.

By submitting a proposal, the Respondent agrees to the terms of SCHEDULE B - PARTICIPATION BY MINORITY AND WOMEN-OWNED BUSINESS ENTERPRISES: REQUIREMENTS AND PROCEDURES. The Respondent must ensure that it and any subcontractors awarded a subcontract for the construction, demolition, replacement, major repair, renovation, planning or design of real property and improvements thereon (the "Work") undertake or continue programs ensuring minority group members and women are afforded equal employment opportunities without discrimination because of race, creed, color, national origin, sex, age, disability or marital status, applying to recruitment, employment, job assignment, promotion, upgrading, demotion, transfer, layoff, termination, and rates of pay or other compensation. The requirement does not apply to (i) work, goods, or services unrelated to the Contract or (ii) employment outside New York State. The Respondent must submit a Minority and Women-owned Business Enterprise and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement, OCSD-1, to ESD with its proposal. If awarded a Contract, the Respondent must submit a Workforce Utilization Report and require each Subcontractor to submit one quarterly during the Contract term in the format required by ESD; pursuant to Executive Order #162, contractors and subcontractors must also report gross wages paid to each employee for work performed on the contract via the Workforce Utilization Report quarterly.

Contractors and subcontractors must report gross wages paid to each employee for work performed on the contract using the Workforce Utilization Report on a quarterly basis, pursuant to Executive Order #162. Under Article 15 of the Executive Law (the "Human Rights Law") and other State and Federal statutory and constitutional non-discrimination provisions, the Contractor and subcontractors must not discriminate on the basis of race, creed (religion), color, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, military status, age, disability, predisposing genetic characteristic, marital status or domestic violence victim status, and must follow the Human Rights Law regarding prior criminal conviction and prior arrest. Failure to comply may result in a finding of nonresponsiveness, non-responsibility and/or breach of the Contract, leading to withholding of funds, suspension or termination of the Contract or other enforcement proceedings. Required forms are Form OCSD-1 (Policy Statement), OCSD-2 (Staffing Plan), OCSD-3 (Workforce Utilization Report), OCSD-4 (Utilization Plan), OCSD-5 (Waiver Request Form) and OCSD-6 (Compliance Report), available at esd.ny.gov links or by request from OCSD@esd.ny.gov.

ESD has determined, pursuant to New York State Executive Law Article 15-A, that assessment of Respondents' diversity practices is practical, feasible, and appropriate. Respondents must include the Diversity Practices Questionnaire (see Appendix B) as part of their response to this procurement. The chunk references Appendix B, which is not included in this chunk.

Article 3 of New York State Veterans' Services Law provides for meaningful participation in public procurement by certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Businesses ("SDVOB"). ESD recognizes the need to promote employment of service-disabled veterans and to ensure certified service-disabled veteran-owned businesses have opportunities for maximum feasible participation in performance of ESD contracts. Respondents are expected to consider SDVOBs in fulfilling the requirements of the Contract, including participation as subcontractors or suppliers, as protégés, or in other partnering or supporting roles.

ESD establishes an overall goal of 6% for SDVOB (Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Business) participation, based on the current availability of qualified SDVOBs. Respondents/Contractors should reference the directory of New York State Certified SDVOBs at https://online.ogs.ny.gov/SDVOB/search; questions on compliance with SDVOB participation goals go to the Designated Contacts. After Contract execution, the Contractor is encouraged to contact the Office of General Services' Division of Service-Disabled Veterans' Business Development at 518474-2015 or VeteransDevelopment@ogs.ny.gov to discuss methods of maximizing SDVOB participation. The Contractor must document "good faith efforts" to provide meaningful participation by SDVOBs as subcontractors or suppliers in performance of the Contract.

Respondents must submit a completed SDVOB Utilization Plan on Form OCSD-4 in accordance with 9 NYCRR § 252.2(i). The Utilization Plan must list the SDVOBs the Respondent intends to use to perform the Contract, a description of the work the SDVOB will perform to meet the Contract goals, and the estimated dollar amounts to be paid to an SDVOB or, if not known, an estimate of the percentage of Contract work the SDVOB will perform. Signing the plan acknowledges that false representations or information showing lack of good faith are prohibited by law and may result in penalties including termination for cause, loss of eligibility to submit future bids or proposals, and/or withholding of payments. Modifications or changes to agreed SDVOB participation after Contract award and during the Contract term must be reported on a revised SDVOB Utilization Plan submitted to ESD. ESD will review the plan and advise the Respondent/Contractor of acceptance or issue a notice of deficiency within 20 days of receipt.

ESD reviews the submitted SDVOB Utilization Plan and advises the Respondent/Contractor of acceptance or issues a notice of deficiency within 20 days of receipt. If a notice of deficiency is issued, the Respondent/Contractor must respond within seven business days of receipt with a written remedy; if the remedy is untimely or inadequate, ESD directs submission of a request for partial or total waiver of SDVOB participation goals on OCSD-5 within five business days of ESD notification, and failure to file the waiver form timely may be grounds for disqualification. ESD may disqualify a proposal as non-responsive if the Respondent fails to submit an SDVOB Utilization Plan, fails to submit a written remedy to a notice of deficiency, fails to submit a request for waiver, or if ESD determines the Respondent failed to document good faith efforts. If awarded a Contract, the Contractor certifies it will follow the submitted SDVOB Utilization Plan for performance of SDVOBs pursuant to the prescribed SDVOB contract goals. Failure to use SDVOBs as agreed in the Utilization Plan constitutes a material breach, entitling ESD to any remedy provided, including a finding of Contractor non-responsibility.

Chunk sets out waiver procedures for New York State minority- and women-owned business enterprise (MWBE) and SDVOB goal requirements. Respondent/Contractor must speak to the Designated Contacts at ESD for guidance before submitting a partial or total waiver request. Under 9 NYCRR § 252.2(m), a Respondent/Contractor able to document good faith efforts to meet the goal requirements (set forth in clause IV) may request a partial or total waiver on Form OCSD-5 with supporting documentation; a waiver request may be submitted at the same time as the SDVOB Utilization Plan, and if not accepted by ESD at that time, clauses II (C), (D) & (E) apply. If documentation is complete, ESD evaluates the request and issues written notice of acceptance or denial within 20 days of receipt. Contractor must attempt in good faith to utilize the SDVOBs identified in its SDVOB Utilization Plan during contract performance; waiver requests after contract award may be made at any time during the contract term but no later than prior to submission of a request for final payment.

Requests for partial or total waiver of established goal requirements made after Contract award may be submitted to ESD at any time during the Contract term, but no later than prior to submission of a request for final payment on the Contract. If ESD reviews the SDVOB Utilization Plan and Monthly SDVOB Compliance Report (OCSD-6) and determines the Contractor is failing or refusing to comply with contract goals with no waiver issued, ESD may issue a notice of deficiency. The Contractor must respond to a notice of deficiency within seven business days of receipt; the response may include a request for partial or total waiver of SDVOB contract goals. Waiver requests should be sent to OCSD.

Per 9 NYCRR § 252.2(n), Contractors must document good faith efforts toward utilizing SDVOBs on the Contract. Required evidence includes: (1) copies of solicitations to SDVOBs and any responses; (2) explanation of specific reasons each responding SDVOB was not selected; (3) dates of any pre-proposal, pre-award or other meetings attended by Contractor, if any, scheduled by ESD with certified SDVOBs ESD determined capable of fulfilling the SDVOB goals set in the Contract; (4) information describing specific steps taken to reasonably structure the Contract scope of work for subcontracting with or obtaining supplies from certified SDVOBs; (5) other information deemed relevant to the waiver request.

Contractor must report Monthly SDVOB Contractor Compliance to ESD during the term of the Contract, covering the preceding month's activity and documenting progress toward the Contract SDVOB goals, per 9 NYCRR § 252.2(q). The report must use form OCSD-6, available on the ESD website, completed by the Contractor. It must be submitted to ESD by the 10th day of each month during the Contract term at OCSD@esd.ny.gov.

The chunk is section X.ix "Encouraging the Use of NYS Businesses in Contract Performance Form" of an ESD contract for commodities, services or technology. Respondents are strongly encouraged and expected to consider New York State businesses in fulfilling the contract requirements. ESD requests that each Respondent complete the Encouraging Use of New York State Businesses in Contract Performance form, accessible at https://esd.ny.gov/sites/default/files/media/document/USEOFNYSBUSINESSES2025.pdf, so ESD can assess the use of New York State businesses in each Proposal.

Contracts resulting from this solicitation are subject to State Tax Law Section 5-a (STL 5-a), which prohibits ESD from approving a contract with an entity that, with its affiliates, subcontractors or affiliates of subcontractors, makes sales in New York State of tangible personal property or taxable services over $300,000 and is not registered for sales and compensating use tax purposes. All Respondents must include a properly completed Form ST220-CA (http://www.tax.ny.gov/pdf/current_forms/st/st220ca_fill_in.pdf) or an affidavit (https://esd.ny.gov/sites/default/files/media/document/STL5A-Affidavit-2025.pdf) stating the Respondent is not required to be registered with the State Department of Taxation and Finance. Proposals without a properly completed ST-220-CA will be considered incomplete and non-responsive and will not be considered for contract award. Only the prime consultant must complete Form ST 220-CA, but Schedule A to Form ST 220-TD requires detailed sub-consultant information such as tax ID number, if applicable, and certificates of authority must be attached by the prime consultant and all subconsultants if applicable. Contracts will require periodic updating of the certifications in Form ST-220-CA.

ESD will prepare a contract after final selection of a Respondent, defining all project terms and conditions and the Respondent's responsibilities in conformance with Schedule A. A sample Schedule A is referenced at https://esd.ny.gov/sites/default/files/ScheduleA-Services_Materials-3818.pdf. Respondents must not submit the information/documentation required by Schedule A with their proposal, aside from information otherwise required by this solicitation. Respondents must thoroughly review Schedule A terms, which are standard for all ESD contracts, and submit any concerns in writing with the Respondent's Administrative Proposal; failure to submit concerns in a timely manner is deemed a waiver of objections, and successful Respondents must accept those terms in the executed contract.

The selected Respondent must provide, at a minimum and to the extent applicable: Commercial General Liability of $1 million per occurrence and $2 million in the aggregate; Commercial Automobile insurance with a limit of not less than $1 million if a vehicle is used in business; Sexual Abuse and Molestation Insurance of $1 million; Worker's Compensation & Employer's Liability insurance at State statutory limits; and Disability insurance coverage at State statutory limits. NYS Urban Development Corporation d/b/a Empire State Development (ESD) must be named as additional insured on a primary and non-contributory basis on the Commercial General Liability and Auto Liability policies. All policies above should include a waiver of subrogation in favor of ESD.

Proposers must provide a completed W-9 form and submit it with the proposal. The chunk references the IRS W-9 form at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fw9.pdf. This is listed under Section X, Contractual Requirements, item xiv, W-9 Form.
